Demos and interface work by other people

I keep finding things other people have made that I want to point at: demos built with HTML-in-canvas, and interface work that isn't built with it and looks like it could be. This is the list. Every entry names who made it and links to where they published it.

A search runs once a week and adds to this page. It reads the sites listed under Where I look, the Open UI minutes and the Chrome release notes, and writes a report on what it found (the reports are in the repository). The best of each week ends up here, and some of it gets rebuilt as a page on this site with a link back to the original. There's an RSS feed of this list.

If you've made something that belongs here, open an issue.

75 entries. Last added to on 23 November 2026.

Made with HTML-in-canvas

Demos by other people that draw live HTML in a canvas.

Margin Dragon

By Baked Design Studio · 29 October 2026 · found through html-in-canvas.dev

A painted dragon moves through a page of HTML text. The text re-flows round it on every frame, and where it breathes fire the page burns away.

No page here changes layout on every frame because of something the canvas draws.

Nearest here: /shape-ui/, /text-notes/

Snowfall

By Baked Design Studio · 29 October 2026 · found through html-in-canvas.dev

Snow settles on live HTML type. You can brush it off, type your own word or start a blizzard.

The snow finds the letters by reading the pixels of the drawn text.

Nearest here: /particles/, /text-labels/

Wishing Pond

By Baked Design Studio · 29 October 2026 · found through html-in-canvas.dev

A web form at the bottom of a koi pond. You type a wish and throw a coin, and ripples and caustics bend the form.

Nearest here: /form-scenes/, /scroll-fx/

<hic-pageflip>

By Bramus · 2 September 2026 · Source

A custom element for a book whose pages curl in 3D when you drag a corner. The text on a page stays selectable and its links work.

The write-up explains the page-curl maths and why a 2D clip looks fake beside it.

Nearest here: /page-book/

Libraries and frameworks

Code you can install that uses the API.

VFX-JS Transitions

By AMAGI · 10 November 2026 · Source

Page transitions through WebGL shaders (glitch, datamosh, pixel sort, slit scan) for any router. It accepts gl-transitions shaders.

It wraps the element in a canvas only while the transition plays. The rest of the time the page is plain DOM.

Nearest here: /transitions/, /nav-shader/

Babylon.js HTML Texture

By Babylon.js · found through Chrome's list

HTML as a texture on a Babylon.js material.

Not tested on this site.

CanvasUI

By DavidHDev · Source

38 components built on the API, for React, Solid, Preact, Vue, Svelte and plain TypeScript. Each is an effect over a page or a block: cloth, heat haze, shatter, peel, glass.

None of its components is a form control.

Nearest here: /shader-css/, /use-it/

PixiJS HTMLSource

By PixiJS · found through Chrome's list

A PixiJS texture source that takes a live element.

Not tested on this site.

PlayCanvas html-texture

By PlayCanvas · found through Chrome's list

HTML as a texture in the PlayCanvas engine.

Not tested on this site.

three.js HTMLTexture

By three.js · found through Chrome's list

A texture whose source is a live element.

Nearest here: /three-form/, /board/

Interface work I'd like to rebuild

None of these use the API. Each is a control or an effect that I think could be rebuilt with a native element drawn by a canvas. The second line of each says how. That line is a plan: I haven't measured any of them.

Glass Slider

By Reijo Palmiste · 20 November 2026 · found through Memorables

A 3D render of a slider. A glass knob pushed along a dark track fills it with light that flares white at the end.

A refraction shader on the thumb of an <input type="range">, with the flare on a float canvas.

Nearest here: /hdr-glow/, /liquid-glass/

Clock Calendar

By Isaiah Trotter · 19 November 2026 · found through Memorables

A day planner on a clock face. You drag the edges of a meeting round the dial to move it.

Two time inputs, or the proposed <rangegroup>. A polar warp is not a matrix, so the pointer would be mapped by script.

Nearest here: /inputs/, /select/

Distortion Waves

By Jakub Antalik · 19 November 2026 · found through Memorables

Confirming a payment pushes a glowing, fringed wave through the card.

A displacement shader over a card with a <button>.

Nearest here: /shader-css/, /scroll-fx/

Swipe to Send

By Yogi Suria · 19 November 2026 · found through Memorables

A payment flow in one WebGL pass. Pushing the button up gathers light under it and ripples in the receipt.

A vertical <input type="range"> and a receipt in a <dl>, under one shader pass.

Nearest here: /scroll-fx/, /nav-shader/

An Infinite Carousel of Cloth Posters

By Jesper Landberg · 17 November 2026 · Source · found through Codrops

Posters are sheets of cloth that drape as you scroll, and the text on a sheet folds with it. WebGPU, with its own scrolling.

With the API each poster could be a real <article> in a native scroller. A link on a draped poster could not be hit until the poster is flat.

Nearest here: /carousel/, /conveyor/

Shader Transition

By saint · 17 November 2026 · found through Memorables

A light to dark switch. A dome of light sweeps up the page and splits the text into colour fringes before it settles.

A picture of the page from captureElementImage(), then a shader mixes old and new after color-scheme changes.

Nearest here: /transitions/, /nav-shader/

Proposed controls and elements

New HTML controls under discussion. A canvas can draw one as soon as a browser has a prototype.

<rangegroup>: a range input with several thumbs

By Open UI (Brecht De Ruyte) · More

A group of range inputs that share one track, with parts you can style. The prototype page has a video trim bar, a meeting slot and opening hours.

On 19 November 2026 the group resolved that nested range groups are not conforming.

Nearest here: /instruments/, /video-lab/

<toolbar>

By Open UI (Luke Warlow)

An element for a group of controls with arrow-key movement between them.

Nearest here: /liquid-glass/

Declarative overscroll actions

By Open UI

A drawer or an action that opens by scrolling past the edge of a scroller, declared in HTML and CSS.

Nearest here: /list-table/

Filterable select

By Open UI (Joey Arhar)

A <select> you can type into to filter its options. Two syntaxes are prototyped in Chromium behind the experimental web platform features flag.

On 12 November 2026 the group settled the focus model: the text field keeps focus.

Nearest here: /select/, /datalist/

Interest invokers

By Open UI

interestfor: an element shows interest (hover, focus, long press) and a popover opens, with no script.

Nearest here: /popovers/, /top-layer/

Menu elements

By Open UI

<menubar>, <menulist>, <menuitem>, <menuitemcheckbox>, <menuitemradio> and <submenu>, with the keyboard behaviour built in.

Nearest here: /popovers/

Richer text fields

By Open UI (Keith Cirkel)

Highlights, ghost text, masking and range information inside <input> and <textarea>.

Nearest here: /caret/, /selection/

Switch attribute

By Open UI (Andres Regalado Rosas)

<input type="checkbox" switch>: a native switch that takes part in forms and can be styled.

Nearest here: /elements/
